messages.subject: Zero inflated regression
parts:
Dear all,

I have been dealing with count data with a zero inflated negative binomial regression, and came across some questions. Could you help to answer my questions?

A part of code as following:

z <- yp$count>0 +0
y <- ifelse(yp$count>0,yp$count,NA)

# INLA formula 
form <-  y ~ 0 + z.b0 + depth.z + secchi.z + geartemp.z + do_gear.z + geardepth.z + f(sz, model=spde, replicate=sz.repl) + y.b0 + depth.y + secchi.y + geartemp.y + do_gear.y + geardepth.y + f(sy, copy='sz', replicate=sy.repl,fixed=FALSE)

result.zinb <- inla(form,family=c("binomial","zeroinflatednbinomial2"),
                    data=inla.stack.data(stk.zy),
                    control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stk.zy),compute=TRUE,link=inla.stack.data(stk.zy)$link),
                    control.inla=list(strategy='gaussian'),
                    control.fixed = list(prec.intercept=1))

I have two questions:
1. I think that this code can analyze the z data using binomial distribution, then the predicted mean value of z is the probability of occurrence (i.e. count is not zero).  Then, it will analyze the count data including zero and non-zero by zeroinflatednbinomial2 and predict count values. Is it correct?
2. I do not fully understand the meaning of "f(sy, copy='sz', replicate=sy.repl,fixed=FALSE)". Is there any difference by using "f(sy, model=spde, replicate=sy.repl)" instead? I ran both codes, and they gave slightly different results.

Thank you!

Ruby

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Zero inflated regression
parts:
First, I think that it is too much to have 'binomial' for occurrence and
'zeroinflatedbinomial2' for the positives. It will be better to use also
'binomial' for the positive part. This gives a king of generalization of
'zeroinflatedbinomial0' for 'count', as you have terms in the linear
predictor for the occurrence as well.

more bellow

On 12/09/2016 09:08 PM, Ruby Ji wrote:
> 1. I think that this code can analyze the z data using binomial
> distribution, then the predicted mean value of z is the probability of
> occurrence (i.e. count is not zero). Then, it will analyze the count
> data including zero and non-zero by zeroinflatednbinomial2 and predict
> count values. Is it correct?
If I understood, you have 'zeroinflatedbinomial2' only for the positives.

> 2. I do not fully understand the meaning of "f(sy, copy='sz',
> replicate=sy.repl,fixed=FALSE)". Is there any difference by using
> "f(sy, model=spde, replicate=sy.repl)" instead? I ran both codes, and
> they gave slightly different results.

Yes, when copying you have a shared field. The other case it is another
field, with its own parameters.

Elias
